title: The villa falls quiet
place: The stone house on Llandough hill, above the River Ely
sources: media register MR-0096 / MR-0097 (Holbrook & Thomas 2005, 'An Early-medieval Monastic Cemetery at Llandough, Glamorgan: Excavations in 1994', Medieval Archaeology 49), p. 86: the villa abandoned in the first third of the 4th century

evidence_links.title: Holbrook & Thomas 2005, An Early-medieval Monastic Cemetery at Llandough, Glamorgan: Excavations in 1994 (PDF)

cast.RB_MOTHER: A woman of about sixty (invented), grey hair bound under a plain wool head-cloth, weathered face, undyed wool dress and a brown cloak pinned with a plain bronze brooch
cast.RB_SON: A man of about thirty (invented), dark cropped hair, short beard, coarse wool tunic, leather belt and a hooded wool cape
cast.RB_CHILD: a child of about six (invented), seen from behind or at a distance only; no lines

cast_rule: New faces for the 4th century: never the c. AD 220 household of door 4, never the 6th-century pair of door 8.
voices_note: Proposed from bible/VOICES.json by gender and age; the movie run confirms them against the voices used in door 4 (a new era means new voices) before any paid call.
setting: s10 (the hill, late Roman): the stone house, its yard and the track down to the Ely
look: Photoreal 16:9 cinematic, Roman Britain, early 4th century AD, inland hilltop in south-east Wales above a winding river and reed marsh, cold clear dawn, muted earthy palette.
negative: No text, no lettering, no heraldry or emblems, no modern objects, invented faces only, no likeness of any real person.
prompt_rule: Each shot's image prompt = look + the shot's image_prompt + negative.
dialogue_rule: The lines carry no facts beyond the source: a household leaves the stone house and does not come back. Why they left is not recorded, so nobody gives a reason. No names: none survives.

moment.place: the stone house on Llandough hill
moment.summary: The last household loads its cart, puts out the hearth and goes down the track to the river. The house stands empty.
moment.basis: The source dates the abandonment to the first third of the 4th century and gives no cause. Chosen as most likely: an orderly departure by a small farming household taking what could be carried (quern, pots, bedding, hens), with the building left standing; later coins and pottery on the hill (door 6) and the late 12th-century barn on the old walls (door 12) both need the walls still to be there.

continuity: Door 4 leaves the stone house newly enlarged; this door empties it. Door 6 (c. AD 375) opens on the same house with its roof partly fallen.

shots.direction: Date-and-place card over a wide dawn shot: a modest single-range stone house with a tiled roof on the hill, a loaded ox-cart standing in the yard, a thin last thread of smoke from the roof. Slow push-in. Ambience: wind, rooks, an ox shifting in its yoke.
shots.image_prompt: Wide shot: a modest single-range Romano-British stone house with a red tiled roof, a two-ox cart loaded with bundles standing in the yard, a thin thread of smoke from the roof, river and marsh far below. No mosaics, no church, no crosses, no sea.

captions.text: Early 4th century AD (c. AD 320) · Llandough hill, above the River Ely · Spoken in modern Welsh, the nearest living language to theirs

shots.direction: Close on hands: the son lashes the load with a hide rope. On the cart a rotary quern, iron cooking pots, rolled bedding, a wicker cage of hens. A child of about six (no lines) sits on the tailboard holding one hen.
shots.image_prompt: Close shot of a man's hands tying a hide rope over a loaded wooden cart: a stone rotary quern, blackened iron pots, rolled wool bedding, a wicker cage of hens; a small child seen from behind on the tailboard.

shots.direction: RB_SON three-quarters to camera beside the cart, speaking to RB_MOTHER in the doorway off-frame; never to the lens.
shots.image_prompt: Medium close-up, three-quarter profile: RB_SON as cast, one hand on a loaded cart, looking off-frame towards a doorway.

lines.speaker: RB_SON
lines.cy: 'Na'r cwbwl, Mam. Ma'r freuan lan, a'r ieir. Dylen ni fod ar yr hewl cyn i'r haul godi dros y coed.
lines.en: That's the last of it, Mam. The quern's up, and the hens. We should be on the road before the sun clears the wood.
lines.es: Es lo último, mamá. Ya subí la muela y las gallinas. Tendríamos que estar en el camino antes de que el sol pase el monte.
lines.accent: South Wales (Welsh standing in for the language of the time)

shots.direction: RB_MOTHER in the doorway, three-quarters to camera, to RB_SON off-frame; she turns back into the house on the last word.
shots.image_prompt: Medium close-up, three-quarter profile: RB_MOTHER as cast, standing in the plain stone doorway of the house, looking off-frame towards the yard.

lines.speaker: RB_MOTHER
lines.cy: Aros. Wna i ddim gadael tân yn llosgi mewn tŷ gwag.
lines.en: Wait. I'll not leave a fire burning in an empty house.
lines.es: Esperá. No voy a dejar un fuego prendido en una casa vacía.
lines.accent: South Wales (Welsh standing in for the language of the time)

shots.direction: Interior. She rakes the hearth out with an iron rake and covers the embers with ash. Bare plastered walls with pale patches where things hung; a swept stone floor; one broken pot left on a shelf. Slow drift.
shots.image_prompt: Interior of a plain Romano-British room: an older woman seen from behind rakes ash over a low hearth; bare plastered walls, swept flagstone floor, an empty shelf with one broken grey pot; grey dawn light from the open door. No mosaics, no painted figures.

shots.direction: RB_MOTHER at the threshold, looking back into the room, speaking over her shoulder to RB_SON off-frame.
shots.image_prompt: Medium close-up, three-quarter profile: RB_MOTHER as cast, at the threshold of an emptied plastered room, half turned back towards the interior.

lines.speaker: RB_MOTHER
lines.cy: Mam fy mam fu'n sgubo'r llawr 'ma. O'n i'n meddwl taw cael 'y nghario mas o 'ma wnelen i, nid cerdded.
lines.en: My mother's mother swept this floor. I thought I'd be carried out of here, not walk.
lines.es: La madre de mi madre barría este piso. Yo pensé que de acá me iban a sacar en andas, no caminando.
lines.accent: South Wales (Welsh standing in for the language of the time)

shots.direction: RB_SON looks up along the eaves, then to RB_MOTHER off-frame.
shots.image_prompt: Medium close-up, three-quarter profile: RB_SON as cast, looking up at the red tiled eaves of a stone house, then off-frame.

lines.speaker: RB_SON
lines.cy: Fe saiff y to am sbel 'to. Fe ddaw rhywun lan am y teils a'r cerrig, siŵr o fod.
lines.en: The roof will stand a good while yet. Someone will come up for the tiles and the stone, I dare say.
lines.es: El techo va a aguantar un buen tiempo todavía. Alguno va a subir por las tejas y la piedra, seguro.
lines.accent: South Wales (Welsh standing in for the language of the time)

shots.direction: He draws the plank door to. There is no lock, only a wooden latch. The child watches from the cart.
shots.image_prompt: Close shot: a man's hand drawing a heavy plank door closed on a wooden latch in a stone doorway; in soft focus behind, a child on a cart watching.

shots.direction: RB_MOTHER, cloak drawn up, beside the cart, to RB_SON at the door off-frame.
shots.image_prompt: Medium close-up, three-quarter profile: RB_MOTHER as cast, cloak drawn up over her head, standing beside an ox-cart in a yard, looking off-frame towards the house.

lines.speaker: RB_MOTHER
lines.cy: Gad y drws ar y glicied. Os daw rhai o'n pobol ni i whilo, gad iddyn nhw 'i gael e ar agor.
lines.en: Leave the door on the latch. If any of ours come looking, let them find it open.
lines.es: Dejá la puerta con el pasador nomás. Si alguno de los nuestros viene a buscar, que la encuentre abierta.
lines.accent: South Wales (Welsh standing in for the language of the time)

shots.direction: Wide. The cart goes down the earth track towards the river and the marsh, the two walking beside the oxen, the child riding. Behind them the stone house stands with no smoke. Ambience: cart wheels, oxen, the hens, wind.
shots.image_prompt: Wide shot from above the yard: a two-ox cart descends an earth track towards a winding river and reed marsh, a man and an older woman walking beside it seen small from behind, a child riding on the load; in the foreground the corner of a stone house with a red tiled roof and no smoke.

shots.direction: The woman looks back once from the turn of the track; the house is small on the brow. She walks on. Seen from behind and at a distance; no close face.
shots.image_prompt: Long shot from behind: an older woman in a brown cloak paused on a hillside track looking back up at a small stone house on the brow of the hill; ox-cart ahead of her on the track.

shots.direction: Hold on the empty yard. Wind moves a shutter; rooks settle on the ridge tiles; wheel ruts in the mud lead out of frame.
shots.image_prompt: Wide still shot of an empty farmyard in front of a single-range stone house with a red tiled roof: wheel ruts in the mud, an open shutter, rooks on the roof ridge, no people, no smoke.

captions.text: The stone house was left in the first third of the 4th century
Why its people left is not recorded
Source: Holbrook & Thomas 2005 (MR-0097). The people and their words are a reconstruction; no name from this household survives.
